Autumn 2026

Equipment partnershipCluj-Napoca, Romania Shooting October 2026
At a glance

One crew. One autumn. Two films that could not be more different.

Film one
Echoes

A chamber thriller. One room, three actors, seven nights. 2.39 anamorphic, an analog look built in camera, every light motivated inside the frame. The hardest kind of small film to shoot well.

Film two
In Their Own Time

A feature documentary. A built studio, location work across a region, a twenty-person unit, seven principal days and a long documentation period. The opposite problem, in the same month.

Interiors at night and daylight on location. A controlled set and a moving one. Whatever equipment goes into this autumn gets tested against both — and both get filmed while it happens.

Film One  ·  Short film
Film one

A veteran hitman breaks in his apprentice over a single night.

While his wife, always in frame and never looked at, prepares her own metamorphosis. A chamber thriller where the cut is the gaze — and what the camera refuses to look at turns out to be the story.

Fifteen minutes. Premiere in Cluj, November 2026, supported by the Cluj City Hall.

How it looks

Warm, worn, at skin temperature. One cold source in the room: the television.

2.39 anamorphic, 16mm grain, an apartment somewhere around 1990 that could be anywhere in the world. A nature documentary runs on the TV throughout — the second film, hiding inside the first.

Practicals inside the frame, a single sodium source through the window, and a camera that stops moving entirely for the last third of the film. Nothing about this is easy to light.

Film Two  ·  Feature documentary
Film two

Every nation has a region it laughs at for being slow.

Romania's is Transylvania. This documentary takes the joke seriously — and finds that the slowness never existed. What existed was measure: a three-hundred-year-old habit of doing things properly, mistaken by everyone else for laziness.

Sixty to seventy minutes. Principal Partner: Cluj County Council.

How it looks

Painted in oil.

Everything the camera cannot reach is rendered in oil: Habsburg Vienna, the guild halls, the scholar bent over his petition. Visible brushwork, warm earth pigments, the palette of the archive itself.

Against it, the filmed world: three voices in a built studio, and location work across a region — a city at rush hour, a village clock still wound by hand, archive rooms with no power to spare.

Production

A Real Crew

CrewA twenty-person film unit. Our own team, not a two-man documentary kit
ShootSeven principal days, plus an extended documentation period across the territory
SetupsA built studio for the three voices, and location work across Cluj and greater Transylvania
PostThe painted build, original score, sound, colour, and an English international master

The camera package is not locked yet.

That is exactly why this conversation is happening now, and not after the shoot. Whatever goes on the truck this autumn is what appears in every frame of both films — and in the lesson we make about it.

What partners receive

A lesson, not a logo.

01
The how-it's-made

A full making-of built around both shoots — how a single interior was lit at night, how a studio was built for three voices, how location work was handled with a twenty-person unit. In English. Your equipment in the hands of a working crew, explained by the people using it.

02
Yours to republish

The making-of and the set stills come to you with the right to use them in full, on your own channels, unedited or re-cut. We are not lending you a mention. We are handing you finished content.

03
Raw material

Behind-the-scenes footage and photography from every shooting day of both films, delivered as usable files, not as a highlight reel we picked for you.

04
Credit

Your name in the end titles of both films, on official materials, and in the communication around every screening. The politeness, after the substance.

Where it goes

Two Audiences

The films — Romania and the circuit
  • Public premiere in Cluj, November 2026, with partner names on stage
  • Romanian streaming platforms and cultural broadcast channels
  • Free across the Romanian cultural circuit — schools, libraries, cultural centres
  • International festival submissions for the short film
The lesson — worldwide
  • In English, on YouTube, no territory
  • Aimed at filmmakers, students and film schools
  • Educational material has a long tail — it is watched for years, not for a week
  • Free for you to republish on your own channels

The films are Romanian. The lesson is not. Your customers are not in the Romanian cultural circuit — they are the people who search for how a film like this was lit and shot. That is the audience we hand you.
